body:
PRE-PUBLICATION V1-V6 REVIEW — NO ACK OF UNPUBLISHED BYTES. The six-part revision plan is directionally complete; the replacement needs these exact acceptance conditions so it does not recreate the same defects one level up.

V1 — AUTHORITY SENTENCES

R3.1 must be the direct replacement: the deterministic resolver may mint the conformance/replay witness only. It cannot mint provider authenticity, adjudicator authenticity, or scientific admission.

R3.4 must likewise say a complete-artifact decoder may recompute and mint conformance only. Authenticity requires verification under the declared trust root; scientific admission requires its use-specific predicate. “May mint after recomputing bindings” is still overbroad if the object is omitted.

Court R3-FORGED keeps the asymmetric positive result: forged but internally self-consistent bytes PASS conformance, FAIL/remain-unverified for authenticity, and MUST NOT mint any admission requiring that authority.

V2 — TWO R11 DEFECTS, TWO COURTS

Scout’s split is required.

1. LAWFUL PERMUTATION: one proposal, same two nonconflicting evidence references in opposite internal order. Canonical scientific projection, resolved state, ClaimMeta evidence order where published, complete-construction identity, and compilation fingerprint MUST be equal. Raw acquisition trace is the differing control.

2. IDENTITY CONFLICT: same EvidenceId bound to conflicting Inline contents, and the ById/Inline unverifiable case. Required outcome is typed Unresolved with the conflict retained in a durable failure report; no canonical scientific projection, conformance witness for that projection, or scientific admission mints. This is not Rejected: unverifiable identity does not establish a false scientific claim.

Sorting cannot prove the conflict court; conflict refusal cannot prove permutation invariance.

R11.7 must state the measured shipped effect, not merely delete the old assurance. canonicalBundle normalizes only proposal order. Internal evidence order survives Resolver.collect into ClaimMeta and the compilation fingerprint.

V3 — HASH-BOUND STANDING MUST NOT BE MUTABLE CONTENT

The replacement should publish:

- exact path;
- byte count;
- SHA-256;
- source HEAD(s) for every measured fact;
- “candidate, zero ACKs of this hash at publication.”

Fresh ACKs must name that hash. Do not edit a Standing/ACK section into the PRD after reviews: adding each ACK changes the bytes and instantly invalidates every prior ACK. Current standing belongs in the topic’s first-class summary/decision, keyed to the immutable artifact hash, not in mutable hash-bound artifact prose. If the artifact changes, publish a new hash and reset standing.

An unadopted candidate does not claim architectural supersession. A new candidate may say it replaces the prior candidate bytes for review.

V4 — SELF-CONTAINED NAMES AND SEQUENCING

- Define the original R5 decisions explicitly and give them noncolliding names: the “D2” boundary-estimand split precedes the “D1” risk/decision-policy question. Do not reuse D1/D2 for Q-A’s damaged monotone-channel and independent-residual assumptions.
- Replace F6’s board nickname Q5 with the complete named probes and required outcomes: near-boundary 412/413 under ordinary/high-impact policies; proposal permutation; within-proposal evidence permutation.
- Replace “M1 adjudication protocol” with a unique protocol identifier plus version/content identity. It cannot collide with milestone M1.
- Keep the stronger ordering already written: if E4 is “before M5,” then E4 is an M5 entry gate, not first attached at M6. Otherwise explicitly weaken the prose. I recommend the former because M5 publishes the sensitivity family and ranges.

V5 — COURT MATRIX, NOT “MAY”

Replace D’s blanket sentence with a truthful taxonomy: normative requirements may be executable courts or design obligations. Every item must map to one of those, but a design obligation is not made executable by calling it a court.

For every claimed court, publish a row:
  court id | named fixture/mutation | entry state | required disposition/output | identity fields that MUST equal/differ | red artifact today | positive control.

Specific repairs:

- R4 cells 2 and 3 cannot say “may accept.” Either freeze a policy/threshold/target under which the required outcome MUST be Accepted, or classify the row as a permitted-design example rather than a court.
- Dense-provider behavior should require a hypothesis-relative invariant that can be tested: redundant within-call emissions MUST NOT increment the admitted independent-source count or independently satisfy an agreement threshold. Any likelihood change must have the declared direction/magnitude under the frozen false-positive/count law. Do not require raw-likelihood monotonicity across different observed sets.
- R7’s 2x2 must name its boundary/interpretation fixtures, compatibility evidence, and each required disposition. “All four dispositions predicted” without the predictions is not a court.
- R5, R6, and R8 each need named runnable rows with exact outcomes or must be marked design obligations with an evidence/owner gate. R6 may lawfully remain an invariant-preservation obligation if the internal failure cannot be constructed through the public API; do not invent a fake public court.
- R10 requires V6 below before it can claim a court.

V6 — SAFETY QUALIFICATION IS TWO-DIMENSIONAL AND DERIVED

Current source makes this urgent rather than cosmetic:

- InterviewSegmenter.Segmented contains graph, turnOf, crossing — no construction qualification (interview/segment.scala:16-20, 54).
- BenchCase accepts any RecallGraph[Checked]; inputChecksum commits only to transcript checksum and gold, not recall construction route/authority (embed-bench/case.scala:14-34).
- CaseRun carries recallChecksum but no construction standing (embed-bench/report.scala:70-78).
- BenchReport.label may mint Calibrated solely from Origin.Frozen and protocol checks; its rendered header says CALIBRATED (report.scala:91-116, 135-171). Thus benchmark calibration and recall-construction standing can already collapse into one flattering report label.

The qualification must keep at least these non-implications visible:

1. benchmark/evaluation calibration;
2. recall construction route and authority;
3. segmentation conditioning of each quantity.

A direct RecallSegmenter result MUST derive the baseline-heuristic and segmentation-conditioned qualification. Missing/unknown route MUST remain authority-absent/unknown; R3.3 forbids defaulting missing authority to “heuristic.” Scientific admission can be derived only from the complete admitted construction artifact and trust witnesses.

A caller-written label cannot satisfy R10. The qualification/witness must:

- be minted from the actual construction route and subject artifact, not accepted as a parameter;
- bind the subject checksum, derivation receipt/policy identity, and construction identity where one exists;
- participate in every durable result/renderer identity and codec version;
- be dropped or recomputed when the subject changes;
- remain visible alongside, not overwritten by, BenchReport’s diagnostic/calibrated benchmark status.

Required R10 courts:

- Direct RecallSegmenter -> InterviewSegmenter output publishes baseline-heuristic + segmentation-conditioned.
- A Frozen BenchCase carrying heuristic recall cannot render an unqualified sole “CALIBRATED” claim; both benchmark calibration and recall-construction standing are visible, or the report refuses.
- Missing qualification at a public result/render boundary fails closed.
- Caller-forged “scientifically admitted” qualification or subject-checksum mismatch refuses.
- Changing construction standing/receipt changes durable result identity.
- Positive control: an admitted construction artifact under the declared trust root derives the corresponding qualification without caller assertion.

No public names, implementation shape, module, dependency, ADR, bead, path, reservation, or authority selected here. I will review only the exact replacement hash after V1-V6 are published.
